While policy interventions aim to ensure equal opportunity, critics argue that superficial reforms may [---1---] existing power structures rather than dismantle them. Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [1] :

Marginalized communities, having experienced repeated cycles of unmet promises, frequently respond with [---3---] skepticism toward institutional narratives of inclusion. Sustainable progress therefore demands a [---4---] commitment to equity—one that confronts systemic barriers instead of merely alleviating their visible symptoms.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [1] :
options_en: reinforce
interrogate
decentralize
neutralize
options_hi: reinforce
interrogate
decentralize
neutralize
questions.solution_en:
Reinforce means to strengthen or entrench something further. The sentence warns that shallow reforms may unintentionally strengthen existing hierarchies instead of challenging them, making reinforce the most precise choice.
WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
• Interrogate implies questioning or examining, the opposite of preserving power structures.
• Decentralize suggests redistribution of authority, not maintenance of dominance.
• Neutralize means eliminate influence, which contradicts the warning tone.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Being a staunch supporter of environmental
conservation, the local NGO nominated
Sarah for the prestigious Green Award.
options_hi: Being a staunch supporter of environmental
conservation, the local NGO nominated
Sarah for the prestigious Green Award.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “Being a staunch supporter” with “As Sarah is a staunch supporter”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Fixing Dangling Participles in the First Part

While most dangling participle errors are fixed by changing the subject after the comma (using passive voice), they can also be corrected in the first part by turning the participle phrase into a dependent clause. This involves adding a conjunction (like As, Because, Since) and a specific subject. This is often necessary when you want to keep the main clause in the active voice.

💢 Application to the Given Question

Being a staunch supporter of environmental conservation, the local NGO nominated Sarah ......

As written, the "NGO" is being called a "staunch supporter." To fix this error in Part A without changing the structure of Part B and C, we must explicitly name the person the phrase refers to. By changing "Being..." to "As Sarah is...", we provide a clear subject for the attribute, thereby removing the grammatical ambiguity.

Corrected Sentence

As Sarah is a staunch supporter of environmental conservation, the local NGO nominated her for the prestigious Green Award.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: Since he was a destitute, Mr. Gupta gave him some money to buy food. (Corrects the original "Being a destitute" error in Part A).

Example 2 ✅: Because the day was rainy, the school management decided to postpone the meet. (Corrects "Being a rainy day" in Part A).

Example 3 ✅: As the room was dark, I could not find my keys. (Corrects "Being dark, I could not find my keys").

No error
options_hi:

questions.solution_en:
✅ Correct Answer - Option A.

Replace “would report” with “would have reported”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Reported Reasoning + Past Hypothetical Outcome (Third Conditional Logic)

When a sentence reports past reasoning, assumption, or inference about outcomes that were also expected in the past, the correct modal structure is: would have + past participle

This reflects an unreal or speculative past result, not a general or present tendency.

💢 Application to the Given Question

“We reasoned that …”

  • Past reporting verb → fixes the reasoning in the past

“…individuals who had frequent indigestion …”

  • Past condition/state

Therefore, the logically expected outcome must also belong to the past hypothetical frame:

  • would have reported ✅

Using would report incorrectly:

  • shifts the meaning toward a present/general tendency
  • breaks tense and conditional consistency

The second clause (would have reported) is already correct, so only Part A is erroneous.

options_en: In its January 1984 edition, the National Geographic

discovered deep inside a remote valley in France.
options_hi: In its January 1984 edition, the National Geographic
magazine explains how ancient cave paintings were
discovered deep inside a remote valley in France.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) replace “explains” with “explained”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Simple Past for Specific Past Events

When a sentence mentions a specific point in time in the past (e.g., In January 1984, Last year, Two days ago, In 1947), the verb must be in the Simple Past Tense (V2).

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...In its January 1984 edition... the magazine explain..."

The time marker "January 1984" is a finished period of time. It acts as an anchor that forces the sentence into the past.

  • Incorrect: ...magazine explain (Present tense implies it happens repeatedly or is a current fact).

  • Correct: ...magazine explained (Past tense reflects the action that occurred when the edition was published).

Corrected Sentence

In its January 1984 edition, the National Geographic magazine explained how ancient cave paintings were discovered deep inside a remote valley in France.

questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Do you recall to meet Arjun and his startup team
at the tech summit in Bengaluru last month, where
they were explaining their AI-based flood-prediction system?
options_hi: Do you recall to meet Arjun and his startup team
at the tech summit in Bengaluru last month, where
they were explaining their AI-based flood-prediction system?
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “to meet” with “meeting”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Gerunds with Verbs of Memory (Recall)

The verb "Recall" is part of a specific group of verbs (including recollect, deny, avoid, and suggest) that must be followed by a Gerund (V{ing}) when they refer to an action. In the context of memory, "Recall" specifically describes looking back at a completed event. Therefore, the action being remembered must be in the noun-form (V_{ing}) rather than the infinitive form (to + V1).

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...Do you recall to meet Arjun and his startup team..."

In this sentence, the context is clearly set in the past ("last month" at a "tech summit"). The speaker is asking the listener to search their memory for a completed action. Because the meeting has already occurred, the grammar requires the gerund "meeting". Using "to meet" is an error because the infinitive typically points toward an intended or future action, which contradicts the meaning of "recall."

Corrected Sentence

Do you recall meeting Arjun and his startup team at the tech summit in Bengaluru last month, where they were explaining their AI-based flood-prediction system?

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ I don't recall seeing any suspicious activity near the building entrance last night.

Example 2 ✅ The witness recollected hearing a loud bang before the lights went out.

Example 3 ✅ She recalled visiting the Swiss Alps during her summer break in 2019.

In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The traveler said, "What a beautiful sunrise this is!"
questions.q_hi:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The traveler said, "What a beautiful sunrise this is!"
options_en: The traveler exclaimed that what a beautiful sunrise that was.
The traveler exclaimed with wonder that it was a very beautiful sunrise.
The traveler exclaimed with wonder that that was a very beautiful sunrise.
The traveler said that that was a very beautiful sunrise.
options_hi: The traveler exclaimed that what a beautiful sunrise that was.
The traveler exclaimed with wonder that it was a very beautiful sunrise.
The traveler exclaimed with wonder that that was a very beautiful sunrise.
The traveler said that that was a very beautiful sunrise.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is Option C: The traveler exclaimed with wonder that that was a very beautiful sunrise.

Key Points

  • The "This" to "That" Rule: In direct speech, the traveller specifically uses the demonstrative pronoun "this" ("...this is"). In standard narration rules for competitive exams, "this" must be converted to "that".

  • Why "It" (Option B) is a Trap:

    • Using "it" makes the sentence sound very natural in spoken English.

    • However, grammatically, "it" is a personal pronoun, while "this" is a demonstrative pronoun. To maintain the exact meaning of the speaker pointing at the sunrise, "that" is the technically correct substitute for "this".

  • The Double "That": Option B remains the most accurate because it includes the conjunction "that" AND the converted pronoun "that."

questions.solution_en:

📌 Rule / Concept: Inversion after "Neither/Nor"

When we want to agree with a negative statement (expressing that someone else also did not do something), we use Neither or Nor followed by an Inversion. The structure must be: Neither/Nor + Auxiliary Verb + Subject.

If the first clause uses "did not," the second clause after "neither" must use the auxiliary "did" before the subject to maintain the negative agreement.

Negative statement :- NEITHER/NOR+HV+SUB

💢 Application to the Given Question

...and neither the shareholders supported the motion...

In the first part of the sentence, the verb is "did not approve" (Simple Past). To show that the shareholders also did not support it, the word "neither" must be followed by the auxiliary verb "did" before the subject "the shareholders". The main verb "support" then returns to its base form.

Corrected Sentence

The board of directors did not approve the proposed expansion and neither did the shareholders support the motion during the annual general meeting held at the corporate headquarters.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: I don't like coffee, and neither does my sister.

Example 2 ✅: They haven't finished the report, and nor have we.

Example 3 ✅: The car wouldn't start, and neither would the tractor.

📌 Rule / Concept: Simple Present for Fixed Future Schedules

💢 Application to the Given Question - The phrase "As per the official itinerary released by the Rashtrapati Bhavan" establishes that this is not a personal or casual plan. options_en: Having neglected by his primary caregivers
during his formative years, the boy struggled
to form stable emotional attachments.
options_hi: Having neglected by his primary caregivers
during his formative years, the boy struggled
to form stable emotional attachments.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “Having neglected” with “Having been neglected”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Passive Perfect Participle (Having + been + V3)

The Perfect Participle (Having + V3) indicates an action completed before the main verb. However, if the subject of the sentence (in this case, "the boy") is the receiver of that action rather than the doer, we must use the Passive form: Having + been + V3.

Using "Having neglected" (Active) would imply the boy neglected someone else, which contradicts the logic of the sentence where he suffered the consequences of being neglected.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"Having neglected by his primary caregivers..."

In this context, the "primary caregivers" are the ones performing the action of neglecting, and "the boy" is the recipient. Because the sentence structure starts with the participle phrase referring to the boy, it must be in the passive voice to show that the neglect happened to him.

Corrected Sentence

Having been neglected by his primary caregivers during his formative years, the boy struggled to form stable emotional attachments.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ Having been defeated in the first round, the team practiced harder for the next season.

Example 2 ✅ Having been told the truth, she felt a sense of immense relief.

Example 3 ✅ Having been repaired twice already, the old car finally broke down for good.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

When the primary strategy failed, the company had to __________ its emergency reserves to sustain operations.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

When the primary strategy failed, the company had to __________ its emergency reserves to sustain operations.
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (2).

English Explanation: “Fall back on” means to rely on something as a backup option when the original plan fails. In the sentence, when the primary strategy failed, the company relied on its emergency reserves to continue operations. Therefore, “fall back on” correctly conveys the idea of using a reserve or alternative resource in times of difficulty. “Fall through” means to fail to happen. “Fall apart” means to break into pieces or collapse emotionally. “Fall out” means to quarrel or to become detached. Since the context refers to depending on emergency reserves as a backup, “fall back on” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Fall through (विफल हो जाना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी योजना का पूरा न हो पाना।
Example: The deal fell through at the last minute. (सौदा आखिरी समय पर विफल हो गया।)

2. Fall back on (सहारा लेना / बैकअप के रूप में निर्भर होना)
Meaning in Hindi: अन्य विकल्प विफल होने पर किसी चीज़ पर निर्भर होना।
Example 1: When his main plan failed, he fell back on his savings to continue his preparation. (मुख्य योजना विफल होने पर उसने अपनी बचत का सहारा लिया।)
Example 2: She always falls back on her experience during tough situations. (कठिन परिस्थितियों में वह हमेशा अपने अनुभव का सहारा लेती है।)

3. Fall apart (टूट जाना / बिखर जाना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी चीज़ का टूट जाना या व्यक्ति का भावनात्मक रूप से टूट जाना।
Example: The old building began to fall apart. (पुरानी इमारत टूटने लगी।)

4. Fall out (झगड़ा होना / अलग हो जाना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी से विवाद हो जाना या अलग हो जाना।
Example: They fell out over a minor issue. (वे एक छोटी सी बात पर झगड़ पड़े।)

options_hi: Multiple irregularities have detected in the procurement process.

Multiple irregularities have been detected in the procurement process.

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C)

📌 Rule / Concept: Present Perfect Tense – Active to Passive Conversion

In the Present Perfect tense, the active structure is:
Subject + has/have + V³ + Object

The passive structure becomes:

Object + has/have + been + V³ (+ by + Subject)

The word “been” is compulsory in Present Perfect passive constructions. The auxiliary (has/have) must agree with the new subject, and the main verb must remain in past participle (V³) form.

Here, “have detected” is in Present Perfect tense.
“Multiple irregularities” is the object and becomes the subject in passive voice. Since it is plural, we use “have”. In passive construction, we must add “been” after “have”, and “detected” remains in V³ form.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

“Been” is mandatory in Present Perfect passive voice.
Always maintain subject–verb agreement after transformation.
Do not remove “have/has” while converting to passive.
Ensure the main verb remains in V³ form.

questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The group of players _______ arriving at the stadium for the final match tomorrow.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (C). Replace the blank with "is".

Rule/Concept: Collective Nouns and Future Arrangements A collective noun (like group) refers to multiple people acting as a single unit. Even when the sentence refers to a future event (indicated by "tomorrow"), we use the Present Continuous tense ("is arriving") to describe a fixed plan or arrangement.

Logic Breakdown:

The Subject: The subject is "The group" (singular). The word "players" is part of the prepositional phrase "of players" and does not influence the verb.

The "Tomorrow" Factor: In English, the present continuous (is/are + verb-ing) is commonly used to talk about scheduled future actions.

Why (D) "was" is incorrect: "Was" is a singular past tense verb. While it matches the singular subject "group," it contradicts the word "tomorrow," which requires a present or future tense.

Why (B) "are" is incorrect: "Are" is plural. It would only be correct if the subject was "The players," but here the subject is the singular "group."
